summary: Eight targeted reference consultations fill important thinker/work gaps, rather than adding more pages on already dominant candidates. This batch is deliberately reference-heavy; the cumulative audit must retain SEP/IEP concentration. Ghazali and Sadra evidence challenges a simplistic Islamic-philosophy decline narrative.
next: Return to independent reviews, non-English philosophy and readers; no further undirected encyclopedia expansion.

sources.title: Rāmānuja
sources.note: Defends real plurality and devotion against rival Vedānta accounts; distinguishes logical, positive and hermeneutic argument rather than treating commentary as passive transmission.
sources.limits: Dates and traditional biographies are uncertain; schools’ own categories require care.

sources.title: Mulla Sadra
sources.note: Explains a synthesis of argument, revelation and mystical insight; situates the Four Journeys and warns that repeated claims about intellectual teachers can outrun historical evidence.
candidates: Transcendent Wisdom in the Four Journeys of the Intellect
sources.limits: Broad influence claims reflect this reference author; synthetic method is not irrationalism.

sources.title: Mary Astell
sources.note: Connects women’s education and marriage criticism with a distinctive Cartesian metaphysics; Christian Religion challenges Locke on thinking matter, but occasionalist attribution requires contextual caution.
candidates: A Serious Proposal to the Ladies
sources.limits: Feminist reputation cannot stand in for the full religious and political position.

sources.title: Tsongkhapa
sources.note: Explains how commentary combines conventional knowledge with emptiness and ethical practice; traces a changing stance toward Yogācāra and Dolpopa rather than a single timeless doctrine.
sources.limits: Commentarial originality assessed separately from textual authority; Tibetan school disagreements preserved.

sources.title: Dharmakīrti
sources.note: Pramāṇavārttika’s nominalism attacks universals; arguments for other minds operate across realist and idealist settings. Reception differs markedly between Tibet, medieval China and modern Japan.
sources.limits: Biography substantially hagiographic; dates debated; verse/commentary genre requires separate nonfiction eligibility.

sources.title: Lady Anne Conway
sources.note: Principles proposes living spiritual substance and moral perfectibility against inert matter; divine justice motivates rejection of eternal punishment. Posthumous anonymous publication complicates visibility.
candidates: The Principles of the Most Ancient and Modern Philosophy
sources.limits: Conway’s monadic language should not be collapsed into Leibniz’s later system.

sources.title: al-Ghazali
sources.note: Rejects a simple anti-philosophy portrait: Incoherence criticizes selected doctrines while Aristotelian demonstration and Avicennian ideas enter theology through al-Ghazali.
candidates: The Revival of the Religious Sciences
sources.limits: Reference overview; later causal interpretations require closer comparison.

sources.title: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
sources.note: Decisive Treatise defends philosophical engagement with scripture through differentiated modes of understanding; commentary and original religious argument both contribute to medieval reception.
sources.limits: Its decline narrative conflicts with evidence for later Islamic philosophy, including Sadra; do not adopt 'last philosopher' literally.
